issues.failure_explanation: The claimed representation is not restricted to τ ≥ 1. Equality up to a positive constant cannot reconcile these values.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the integral representation only for τ ≥ 1 and retain the already supplied explicit formula for τ = 0.
issues.overall_effect: The background integral representation is invalid for zero-order Wendland kernels; the later collocation results use larger τ.
issues.title: The alternative Wendland integral does not cover the admitted case τ = 0
issues.why_classification: A local case distinction restores a valid representation for every kernel without changing the collocation method or its advertised parameter regime.

issues.failure_explanation: For the admitted case (d,τ) = (1,0), the definition gives Φ(x) = (1−|x|)+. This kernel is the convolution of two unit-interval indicators and has Fourier transform (sin(ξ/2)/(ξ/2))². Its native-space norm therefore has a reciprocal spectral weight singular at every nonzero multiple of 2π. A Gaussian belongs to H¹ but its nonzero Fourier transform makes that native-space norm infinite. Thus both the asserted space equality and norm equivalence fail in this case.

issues.failure_explanation: The half-relaxed limit is local, whereas this supremum is over a noncompact spatial domain. A strict global maximum supplies no uniform gap at infinity. For example, uniformly smooth bounded bumps escaping to spatial infinity have zero local half-relaxed limit, but their global maxima need not approach a contact point of that limit with a noncoercive test function. Thus the asserted global near-maximizing sequence does not follow from the stated premises.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Select local approximate maximizers on a fixed compact space-time cylinder around the strict contact point and prove their convergence using compactness and strictness. The later comparison uses only that neighborhood.
issues.overall_effect: The sequence needed for the viscosity comparison is not justified, so the subsolution argument has a localization gap.
issues.title: Local half-relaxed convergence does not supply the claimed global near-maximizers
issues.why_classification: Standard local maximum selection repairs the proof without changing the scheme, assumptions, rate, or convergence conclusion.

issues.failure_explanation: Choose two nearest nodes, distance 2Δ₂x apart, and nodal data bounded by one taking values +1 and −1 there. Interpolation and the mean value theorem force sup|∇I(g)| ≥ 1/Δ₂x. The claimed coordinate-derivative bound instead gives sup|∇I(g)| ≤ √d C, contradicting Δ₂x → 0. This is also incompatible with fixed Lipschitz data: uniform second-derivative bounds and dense interpolation would force a cusp such as min(|x₁|,1) to have a continuously differentiable limit. No inverse-entry condition can remove these interpolation constraints.

issues.failure_explanation: The multi-index sum counts each mixed second derivative once, whereas the declared Frobenius norm counts both symmetric entries. Thus the hypothesis need not imply |D²φ| ≤ C₁. Concretely, on O = (−ε,ε)² take φ(y) = a y₁y₂ with a = C₁/(1+ε)² > C₁/√2. Its stated derivative sum equals C₁, but its Hessian has norm √2a > C₁. For F(γ) = −tr γ, the quadratic game's value divided by δ tends to max{tr γ: γ ≤ D²φ(0), |γ| ≤ C₁} = √(C₁²−a²)−a < 0, while the claimed target is zero. The error is therefore of order δ, not δ^(1+β).
